scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC4 and PC5 (Location A VLAN 10, 172.16.10.0/24) report they
cannot reach their gateway (172.16.10.1) any more. Laptop0
on VLAN 20 in the same Location is unaffected. Find the
broken link in the L2 path.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: mswitch1 eth0.10 (VLAN 10 trunk subif
  toward router0)
Mechanism: mswitch1 has separate per-VLAN trunk subinterfaces
  for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20. PC4/PC5's gateway (router0
  eth0.10 at 172.16.10.1) sits on the far side of this
  trunk. With eth0.10 down on mswitch1, no VLAN 10 frames
  reach router0 — ARP and ping both fail. VLAN 20 uses
  eth0.20 which is unaffected.
Localization: mswitch1
Root cause: eth0.10 trunk subinterface administratively down
Fix: `ip link set eth0.10 up` on mswitch1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth0.10 up` on mswitch1

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a downed VLAN sub-interface on mswitch1, specifically `eth0.10` — the 802.1Q VLAN 10 sub-interface created over `eth0` (the trunk port that connects mswitch1 to switch1 on the `link_msw1_sw1` segment).

**Mechanism:** switch1 bridges PC4 and PC5 (both on `br_vlan10`) toward mswitch1 via the VLAN 10-tagged sub-interface `eth0.10`. On mswitch1, `eth0.10` is configured as a member of `br_vlan10`, which in turn connects to `eth4.10` (the VLAN 10 trunk leg toward router0). Router0's `eth0.10` carries the gateway IP 172.16.10.1/24. Because mswitch1's `eth0.10` has no UP flag and its kernel state is DOWN, no VLAN-10 frames from switch1 can enter mswitch1's VLAN 10 bridge domain. Every ARP request from PC4/PC5 for 172.16.10.1 dies here; router0's ARP reply never crosses back. PC4 confirms this: `arp -n` shows `172.16.10.1 (incomplete)`.

**Why laptop0 is unaffected:** Its VLAN 20 counterpart, `mswitch1.eth0.20`, is fully UP (`<BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP>`), so the VLAN 20 path through mswitch1 is intact and laptop0 reaches 172.16.20.1 with 0% packet loss.

**Root cause:** `mswitch1.eth0.10` was not brought up (missing `ip link set eth0.10 up` in the startup configuration), leaving the VLAN 10 trunk sub-interface in the DOWN state while VLAN 20 was correctly initialised.

**Corrective fix:** Run `ip link set eth0.10 up` on mswitch1 to restore the VLAN 10 sub-interface. To survive reboots, add this command to mswitch1's startup script alongside the existing `ip link set eth0.20 up`.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies mswitch1 as the affected device in multiple places.
The agent explicitly identifies mswitch1's VLAN 10 trunk sub-interface eth0.10 as the affected component.
The report clearly identifies VLAN 10 (eth0.10) as down and causing the failure while noting VLAN 20 (eth0.20) is up and unaffected.
The agent recommends bringing up eth0.10 with 'ip link set eth0.10 up' on mswitch1 (and persisting it), which matches the expected fix.
